Judgment:

This appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award and decree dated 13.06.2005 in M.V.O.P.No.850 of 2002 on the file of the Motor Vehicles Accidents Claims Tribunal -cum- X Additional District Judge (F.T.C.), Guntur at Narasaraopet.

sentences.text: For the purpose of convenience, the parties are arrayed as before the Tribunal.

04. The case of the claimants is briefly as follows:
a) On 23.03.2002, at about 06.00 A.M., while Bathula Venkateswarlu (in short 'deceased') was coming in a mini lorry bearing No.AP 27 T 8766 with a bag of rice by paying Rs.20/- as fare for rice bag, the mini lorry collided with a R.T.C. bus bearing No.AP 9 Z 5196 near Venugopalaswami Rice Mill, Durgi Village due to the rash and negligent driving of drivers of both vehicles.
The deceased and another person died on the spot and others sustained severe injuries.
A case in Crime No.15/02 under Section 304-A I.P.C. was registered by the police.

The deceased was an agriculturist and was earning Rs.30,000/-
p.a.
He was the only earning member of his family.
The claimant No.1 is wife, the claimant No.2 is daughter and the claimant No.3 is minor son of the deceased.
The claimants filed the petition against the three respondents contending that they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- to the claimants.
b) The respondent No.2 remained ex parte.
c) The respondents No.1 and 3 filed separate written statements.

d) The respondent No.1 contended that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the bus and that the mini lorry was coming in opposite direction with high speed in the middle of the road and that observing the same, the driver took the bus to the left margin of the road and took all other precautions, yet, the mini lorry dashed against the bus causing severe damage to the bus.
It is also contended that the compensation claimed by the claimants is excessive and that the respondent No.1 is not liable to pay any compensation.

e) The respondent No.3 filed written statement opposing the claim stating that the driver of the mini lorry didn't possess valid driving license at the time of the accident; that the lorry is a goods vehicle and cannot carry passengers on hire or reward or gratuitously; that the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation as the insurer of the vehicle violated the terms of insurance policy.
It was further pleaded that the claimant No.2 is a major and married woman residing with her husband and not a dependent and so she is not entitled to any compensation.
This respondent placed the burden on the claimants to prove their case and also the age, occupation and yearly income of the deceased.
It was also pleaded that the amount of compensation claimed is excessive and prayed to dismiss the petition.

05. On behalf of the claimants, the claimant No.1 got herself examined as P.W.1 and following documents were marked:
 Ex.A1 C.C. of F.I.R.
 Ex.A2 C.C. of inquest report.
 Ex.
A3 Post-mortem report.

sentences.text:
On behalf of the respondents, D.V.S.M.N. Rao was examined as R.W.1 and insurance policy was marked as Ex.B1.
07.
After considering the evidence of both parties, the Tribunal held that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the mini lorry only.

It came to the said conclusion by holding that the driver of the bus was examined to deny the rash and negligent driving and his evidence stood the test of credibility, whereas the driver of the mini lorry was not even examined to deny the allegations against him and moreover the preliminary proceedings were also in support of the evidence of R.W.1.

It was further observed that as per Section 163-A of the M.V.
Act, claimant is not required to prove rash and negligent driving of the driver of the crime vehicle.

08. The Tribunal observed that the claimants could not place evidence in proof of the actual income of the deceased and therefore, the notional income of the deceased was fixed at Rs.15,000/- p.a. as per the relevant item-6 of Schedule-II of the M.V. Act and then deducted 1/3rd of such income towards personal expenses of the deceased and multiplied the same by '11' applicable to the persons aged between 50 to 55 and therefore, the total amount of Rs.1,10,000/- was awarded.
In addition thereto, Rs.15,000/- was awarded towards consortium to the wife of the deceased.
Further, an amount of Rs.10,000/- was awarded as per Item-3, Schedule-II towards loss of estate and Rs.5,000/- towards funeral expenses.
Thus, in all, the claimants were held entitled to compensation of Rs.1,40,000/- with interest @9% p.a. with proportionate costs from the date of the petition till the date of realization.

09. Accepting the contention of the insurance company that there is violation of condition of insurance policy for carrying passenger in a goods vehicle, the Tribunal exempted the insurance company / respondent No.3 from the liability and made the respondent No.2 alone liable to pay compensation, however directed the insurance company to first pay to the claimants and then recover the amount from the respondent No.2.

10. Aggrieved by the award and decree, this appeal was preferred by the insurance company mainly contending that the Tribunal, having observed that there is no liability for the insurance company,
ought not to have fastened liability on it to pay the amount of compensation to the claimant and then recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.
It was further contended that the Tribunal ought to have considered that there was contributory negligence of the driver of the R.T.C. bus.
The same grounds were reiterated during the course of arguments.
11. The learned counsel for the claimants and the A.P.S.R.T.C. supported the award and requested not to interfere with the same.

sentences.text: The main grievance of the appellant / insurance company is that it is no way liable to pay compensation since the deceased was a gratuitous passenger and not covered by the policy of insurance and having held so, the Tribunal erred in fastening liability on the insurance company.
13. The evidence on record shows that the Tribunal also observed that the deceased also travelling along with a bag of rice, however further observed that he paid Rs.20/- for rice bag.
Thus, it would amount that the deceased was travelling along with goods either as owner or agent of its owner and therefore, he is not mere gratuitous passenger or passenger by paying fare.
Therefore, the insurance company cannot disown its liability.
As the claimants or the respondent No.2 have not challenged the observation of the Tribunal, there is no need to examine the question whether the insurance company is totally liable or not.

Since the Tribunal ordered the insurance company to first pay and gave it liberty to recover the said amount from the respondent No.2, this Court does not see any reason to interfere with such finding of the Tribunal.
14. In the result, the Motor Accident Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.

Interim orders granted earlier, if any, shall stand vacated.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
JUSTICE B.S. BHANUMATHI Date: 07.08.2025 NSM The Honourable Ms. Justice B.S.Bhanumathi
